title: After-hours joints on Central Avenue
summary: Pearl's, Nell's Rendezvous and others where musicians drank and ate after work.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: No, this is way before Lovejoy had a
place. No, Lovejoy didn't come into it until World War II time. We had, after-hour joints we used to go to, where we could buy whiskey after hours and meet the girls.
But where were they? What were their names? Do you remember?
Oh, Pearl's and, you know, the --
Oh, that was behind the Dunbar Hotel, next to the alley, one of them kind of places, you know, and we had places -- Nell's Rendezvous and --

Central Avenue, way out around 45th, 46th Street. You could stay there until ten o'clock in the morning, buy whiskey and have chitlings sometimes and fried chicken, hot biscuits and honey, different things like that, you know.
